title: Chain-complex construction from a left resolution
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a category with zero morphisms (every $\mathrm{Hom}(Y,Z)$ has a distinguished element $0$ with $g\circ 0=0$ and $0\circ f=0$), and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful. For a left-resolution datum $\Lambda=(F,\pi)$ for $\iota$ [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-api] (a functor $F:A\to C$ and a natural transformation $\pi:\iota F\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ with epimorphic components), Mathlib's declaration `CategoryTheory.Abelian.LeftResolution.chainComplexFunctor` constructs a functor $A\to\operatorname{ChainComplex}(C,\mathbb N)$. At an object $X$, its degree-$0$ term is $F(X)$, its degree-$1$ term is $F(\ker(\pi_X))$, and for $n\ge0$ its degree-$(n+2)$ term is $F(\ker\iota(d_{n+1,n}))$; the differential $d_{1,0}$ is the unique map with $\iota(d_{1,0})=\pi_{\ker\pi_X}$ followed by the inclusion $\ker\pi_X\to\iota F(X)$, and $d_{n+2,n+1}$ the unique map with $\iota(d_{n+2,n+1})=\pi_{\ker\iota(d_{n+1,n})}$ followed by the kernel inclusion (`map_chainComplex_d_1_0`, `map_chainComplex_d`). On a morphism $f:X\to Y$ it is $F(f)$ in degree $0$ and $F$ of the induced kernel maps in higher degrees.
